summary: Session cohort fragmentation after async rollout commit causes pinned-version divergence and fallback churn
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a burst of fallback responses and mixed-model outputs for a subset of sessions immediately following a scheduled async rollout commit for a new canary variant. Impact: about 4% of NexaDocs tenant sessions in us-east-1 experienced repeated fallbacks to the legacy variant for 8–12 minutes; a subset saw alternating responses (new vs legacy) within the same logical session.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency spikes and inconsistent completions for multi-turn chat flows.
- Temporary elevated token costs due to duplicate requests retried by the frontend.
- Severity: P1 (customer-visible degradation on dedicated plan).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-3, tenant: nexadocs-prod, region: us-east-1
- Model: gptx-3.2-quant (new canary: gptx-3.2-quant-v2)
- Orchestrator version: route-coordinator v1.14.3 (deployed at 03:12 UTC)
- Edge sidecar/ingress: edge-proxy v2.4.1

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) During the scheduled canary commit window (03:12–03:20 UTC) the orchestrator applied an async commit to promote v2 for 10% traffic slice.
2) Prewarm succeeded; canary healthchecks green.
3) ~03:15 UTC: subset of sessions see a fallback to legacy variant despite previously pinned version.
4) Affected sessions show rapid alternation: requests A->v2, B->v1, next request A->v1 (same session).

Logs/Telemetry references:
- Support trace: trace-id=tr-9f3b2c (attached)
- Edge logs: edge-proxy shows 502-to-200 handoffs correlated with token TTL refill events (query log: edge.query('tenant:nexadocs AND ts:[2026-03-10T03:12 TO 2026-03-10T03:30]')).
- Orchestrator events: snapshot-commit at 03:12:45 UTC, async-commit ack at 03:13:02 UTC, cohort-resync attempts 03:14:xx -> 03:18:xx.

Customer notes:
- NexaDocs reported users seeing inconsistent answers in active documents; they increased retries on the client to mask flakiness which amplified traffic briefly.

Requested by customer: quick mitigation and post-incident explanation.
comments: 2026-03-10 04:00 - Support (Aisha Patel): Opened ticket after NexaDocs support call. Collected traces and asked for immediate mitigation. Notified SRE on #support and #incidents.

2026-03-10 04:12 - SRE (Diego Ramos): Observed cohort-resync floods from orchestrator. Hypothesis: async commit ordering left a partial cohort map that edge-sidecar used to route, producing per-connection sticky mismatches.

2026-03-10 05:05 - Eng (Rachel Chen): Confirmed orchestrator emitted overlapping snapshots (seq 452/453) and edge caches accepted seq 452 then 453 then reverted to 452 due to late prewarm TTLs. Possible race between prewarm-complete and commit-ack sequence numbers.
2026-03-10 05:40 - Support (Aisha Patel): NexaDocs applied a client-side workaround: disable aggressive retry and reduce keepalive churn; reported improvement but still intermittent divergences.

2026-03-11 09:20 - SRE (Diego Ramos): Temporary mitigation applied: forced cohort rebind for nexadocs-prod via orchestrator admin endpoint (admin/rebind?tenant=nexadocs-prod). Early telemetry: drop in fallback rate from 4% -> 0.4%.

2026-03-12 14:30 - Eng (Liam O'Connor): Creating follow-up epic to harden commit ordering. Will propose short-term control-plane guardrail (block commit until all prewarm acks across slice are consistent).

2026-03-12 15:00 - Customer (NexaDocs - ops@nexadocs.com): Thanks for the quick response. Please confirm whether there will be a config we can set on dedicated pools to avoid this during our next scheduled rollout.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Reproduced in staging by replaying orchestrator commit sequence against dp-us-east-3; observed that edge proxy caches accepted snapshot seq N, then N+1, then due to delayed 'cohort-commit-ack' some workers reverted to previous in-memory routing map during a transient resync.
- Root cause hypothesis: async rollout path allows snapshot seq gaps when prewarm acks arrive out of order. Edge sidecar code attempts to reconcile by picking lowest seq when it detects conflict which can flip session pins mid-flight.
- Query snippets used:
  * ES: GET /logs/_search?q=trace-id:tr-9f3b2c AND orchestrator.commit.seq:[451 TO 455]
  * Orchestrator metrics: histogram(commit_apply_latency) shows 95th=4.6s during window; prewarm ack latency 99th=6.2s
- Additional anomaly: token rotation (session cookie refresh) happened ~03:16 UTC for some clients; this coincided with an edge-sidecar cache invalidation path that triggers a routing recalculation and may have interacted with the seq flip.
- Affected cohort size primarily sessions with sticky-cookie version v1 format (older cookie shape used by NexaDocs web client).

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Forced rebind (admin/rebind) reduced fallback churn.
- Applied edge-sidecar patch to treat out-of-order seq as 'deferred' rather than 'accept lower seq' to avoid flip; patch rolled to 10% of dp-us-east-3 and validated for 6h in canary.

Open questions:
- Why did orchestrator emit overlapping snapshots rather than a linear chain? Is there a commit race when separate control-plane replicas apply the same change?
- Does the prewarm ACK and commit ACK ordering guarantee need to be tightened?
resolution:
Workaround and next steps:
- Workaround implemented: forced cohort rebind for affected tenant (admin/rebind) and rolled a sidecar change to defer acceptance of lower-sequence snapshots. Both reduced customer impact.
- Short-term code change merged to route-coordinator: add commit gating until prewarm acks observed for all targeted workers (PR: https://github.com/redwood/route-coordinator/pull/842). Patch will be included in v1.14.4.
- Follow-ups assigned: ENG-SECURE-COMMIT-ORDER (hardening control-plane commit sequencing), SRE-VERIFY-ROLLBACK-PLAYBOOK (update runbook to include admin/rebind step).
- Customer communication: Customer notified 2026-03-12 16:00 UTC with summary and expected patch schedule. SLA credit assessment in progress per dedicated contract.

Status: Mitigated (fallback rate returned to baseline). In Progress for permanent fix and runbook updates.
